note: When two Grace Hill sources disagree, this is where it gets recorded and resolved. Ruth asked how the system decides which source is authoritative when sources conflict. The honest answer was that it had no mechanism — it took whichever source it read last. This file is that mechanism.
why: A conflict resolved silently is worse than a conflict left open, because the losing source stays live for whoever reads it next. Recording the conflict means the person who finds the stale document knows it is stale.
rule: Rank decides, and the resolution is written down. Where rank alone cannot settle it — two rank-1 sources disagreeing — it goes to the VP of Product Marketing and stays UNRESOLVED in the app until she rules. An unresolved conflict is shown to reps as a caution, never averaged into a confident middle.

conflicts.subject: All-party recording-consent state list for mystery shopping
conflicts.resolution: 14 is correct. GHU 1060 and 1061 win on agreement between two sources of equal rank against one.
conflicts.repFacing: Use 14 states including Oregon. If you land on GHU 1623 it is short by one and is being corrected.

howToAdd: Any task that finds two Grace Hill sources disagreeing adds an entry here rather than picking a winner quietly. If rank settles it, resolve it and say which rank won. If it does not, mark it unresolved and write the repFacing line so a rep has something safe to say in the meantime.
scopeNote: A conflict is shown on a competitor record only when it touches a product line that record overlaps. A caution that appears on all 98 pages is wallpaper, and wallpaper is what people stop reading.
